target_customer: ERPs, fintechs, accounting and financial management software companies in Brazil that need bank data and Pix payments through one API
problem: Brazilian software companies could not reliably read customers' bank and broker data or initiate payments. Pluggy provides an Open Finance API, described as Plaid for Brazil.
business_model: Usage-based and subscription API fees for data connectors and Pix payment initiation

founders.name: Federico Miras
founders.role: Co-founder, Head of Product and CEO
previous_startups: Created first software company at 19 (per YC bio, outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: Argentinian tech entrepreneur and programmer per YC page.

founders.name: Rogerio Correa
founders.background_notes: 10 years in business consulting and 3 years in digital transformation consulting per YC page.

founders.name: Victor Braga
founders.background_notes: Worked in banking and M&A consultancy per YC page.

founders.name: Bruno Loiola
founders.background_notes: Role from a startup profile found via search; YC page gives no bio.

competitors.name: Belvo
competitors.what: Open finance API platform for Latin America with a Brazil expansion
competitors.traction_then: Opened a Sao Paulo office in 2020
competitors.funding_then: $10M raised for Brazil expansion per Fintech Futures (2020)

technical_complexity.rationale: Connecting to many banks before regulated Open Finance meant per-bank integrations and reliability work, which is hard but standard for a small team. Later regulatory payment initiation raised the bar.

defensibility.rationale: Coverage breadth, embedded integrations in ERPs and the central bank authorization as a payment initiator (June 2024) add stickiness, but several rivals offered similar APIs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. Rivals stayed independent in the sources found, and Pluggy reports breakeven in 2024.

market_need_then: Brazil was rolling out regulated Open Banking from 2021 and software vendors wanted bank data access. Pluggy claimed to cover 90 percent of Brazilian bank accounts on its YC listing.

identity.logo: Wordmark where the U is drawn as a plug with a trailing wire, topped by a sun symbol, in sunshine yellow on white, per a DesignRush blog interpretation
identity.voice_and_tone: Simple and fast: sandbox to first request in 5 minutes

branding.brand_signature: Plaid for Brazil positioning and the plug-shaped logo

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable plug-themed name and logo and wide Brazilian fintech press coverage of its rounds, but no evidence of merch or a community beyond developers.

pivots.why: Obtained central bank authorization as a payment transaction initiator in June 2024 per Finsiders Brasil.

outcome_analysis: Pluggy rode Brazil's regulated Open Finance rollout, raised small rounds and reports breakeven since 2024 with about 500 direct clients. Its capital efficiency is notable, with only about $6M raised by 2026 per press, and its payment initiation license adds a regulatory edge. Rivals such as Belvo and Quanto raised far more.
notes: The pre-seed was reported as more than R$3 million, no USD figure given, so amount_usd is null. The seed is reported by LatamFintech and Startupi as about R$10M or US$1.9M, with Seedtable dating it to May 2022 and listing Y Combinator; other investors not verified. Series A is confirmed by many outlets (Startups.com.br, Finsiders Brasil, Intellinews, Dealroom, LatamList) with announcement on Aug 26 2026. Total raised about $6M per press, while CB Insights lists $3.57M over nine rounds and a Startup Researcher item cites a $2.5M seed in 2021, so figures conflict. Quanto and Pismo were also rivals but their sources are undated, so they are not listed. Founder education and prior employers are only partly stated on the YC page.
